title: STRANGE MINUTE #19 · WHAT IF

lines.text: What if Jupiter replaced our Moon?
Same distance as the Moon, but forty times wider.
It would swallow a huge chunk of the night sky.
It's about 26,000 times heavier than the Moon.
lines.say: It's about twenty-six thousand times heavier than the Moon.

lines.text: So its pull on our oceans would be 26,000 times stronger.
lines.say: So its pull on our oceans would be twenty-six thousand times stronger.

lines.text: Want proof? Jupiter's moon Io orbits at almost that distance.
Jupiter squeezes it so hard, Io has over 400 active volcanoes.
lines.say: Jupiter squeezes it so hard, Io has over four hundred active volcanoes.

lines.text: Earth's crust could crack and spill lava, just like Io.
And Jupiter's deadly radiation belts would wrap around our planet.
At least the view would be epic: a storm bigger than Earth.
So, would you trade the Moon for Jupiter?
